Convert a GFF3/GTF Annotation to Parquet Files

Source: R/annotation.R
prepare_isoformic_annotation.Rd

Parses a GENCODE/Ensembl style GFF3 or GTF annotation file with DuckDB in a single pass and writes one Parquet table per feature level (genes, transcripts, exons) plus metadata and sequence-region tables into an annotation directory. This directory is what IsoformicExperiment objects point to through their annot_path property.

Usage

prepare_isoformic_annotation(
  input_path,
  output_path = NULL,
  file_type = c("auto", "gff", "gtf"),
  annot_name = NULL,
  overwrite = FALSE,
  haplotype = NULL
)

Arguments

input_path

Path to a GFF3 or GTF file, optionally gzip-compressed.

output_path

Directory under which the annotation directory is created. NULL (default) uses get_isoformic_cache().

file_type

"auto" (default) detects the format from the file extension; otherwise "gff" or "gtf".

annot_name

Name of the annotation directory. Defaults to the input file name, lower-cased, with dots replaced by underscores.

overwrite

Logical. Re-create the annotation directory even if a complete one already exists.

haplotype

Optional label (for example "maternal" or "hap1") stored in the haplotype column of every table, for annotations of one haplotype of a phased assembly. See merge_annotations().

Value

The path to the annotation directory (character string).

Details

Reading a full human GENCODE release (about 3 million features, gzip-compressed) takes a few seconds; the result is cached so repeated calls with the same file and output location return immediately.

The parser is vocabulary-agnostic so that annotations from different providers and assemblies work the same way:

  • GENCODE GFF3/GTF (GRCh38, GRCm39): gene/transcript/exon features with gene_id, transcript_id, gene_type, transcript_type.

  • Ensembl and Ensembl Rapid Release GFF3 (e.g. T2T-CHM13 GCA_009914755.4): ncRNA_gene, mRNA, lnc_RNA, ... features, gene:/transcript: prefixed IDs, biotype, rank.

  • NCBI RefSeq GFF3 (e.g. GCF_009914755.1_T2T-CHM13v2.0): gene-/rna- prefixed IDs, gene_biotype, mRNA/lnc_RNA/miRNA features and pseudogenes carrying exons directly.

  • T2T consortium Liftoff and CAT/Liftoff GFF3 (RefSeq or GENCODE lifted to CHM13) and HPRC per-haplotype CAT annotations: transcript_biotype, gbkey, and the source_gene / source_transcript attributes, kept as source_gene_id / source_transcript_id so that lifted annotations can be mapped back to the GRCh38 GENCODE or RefSeq identifiers.

  • MANE GFF3/GTF and CHESS GFF3 (same vocabulary as GENCODE/RefSeq).

  • FANTOM CAT (FANTOM5 lv1-lv4) and FANTOM6 CAT GTF: __na placeholders become NA, geneClass is used as the gene (and, when the transcript has no type, the transcript) type, and geneCategory, DHS_type, coding_status, cumulative_support and TIEScore are kept. CAGE cluster identifiers come from the FANTOM ID mapping table, see add_fantom_cat_tables().

  • StringTie, Bambu, FLAIR, IsoQuant and SQANTI3 GTF files from long-read or assembled transcriptomes: reference_id/cmp_ref, ref_gene_id and ref_gene_name populate the source identifiers and gene names; novel transcripts without a biotype get transcript_type = NA until add_sqanti_classification() assigns SQANTI3 structural categories.

Genes are features of a gene-like type or parents of transcripts; transcripts are features of a transcript-like type or parents of exons. Transcript types are normalised (mRNA to protein_coding, lnc_RNA to lncRNA) and fall back to the feature type (miRNA, snRNA, ...) when no biotype attribute exists.

  • genes: gene_id, gene_name, gene_type, source_gene_id, gene_class, gene_category, dhs_type, coding_status, cumulative_support (FANTOM CAT attributes, NA elsewhere), haplotype, seqid, start_pos, end_pos, strand.

  • transcripts: transcript_id, transcript_name, transcript_type, gene_id, source_gene_id, source_transcript_id, tags (comma-separated tag attributes such as MANE_Select, basic, Ensembl_canonical), is_canonical (TRUE for MANE Select, Ensembl canonical or RefSeq Select transcripts), coding_status (FANTOM CAT), transcript_support_level (GENCODE TSL), tie_score (FANTOM CAT TIEScore), cds_start, cds_end, cds_length (aggregated from the CDS features; NA for non-coding transcripts), haplotype, seqid, start_pos, end_pos, strand, n_exons, tx_length.

  • exons: exon_id, transcript_id, exon_number, haplotype, seqid, start_pos, end_pos, strand.

  • metadata: key, value (source file, format, header pragmas, creation time).

  • seq_regions: seqid, start_pos, end_pos.

Examples

gff <- system.file("extdata", "example.gff3", package = "isoformic")
annot_dir <- prepare_isoformic_annotation(gff, output_path = tempdir())
#> ℹ Using cached annotation directory /tmp/Rtmp2Tt1au/example.
list.files(annot_dir)
#> [1] "annot_data_exons.parquet"       "annot_data_genes.parquet"      
#> [3] "annot_data_transcripts.parquet" "annot_metadata.parquet"        
#> [5] "annot_seq_regions.parquet"     
head(read_parquet(file.path(annot_dir, "annot_data_transcripts.parquet")))
#> # A tibble: 6 × 21
#>   transcript_id     transcript_name transcript_type gene_id       source_gene_id
#>   <chr>             <chr>           <chr>           <chr>         <chr>         
#> 1 ENST00000282397.9 FLT1-201        protein_coding  ENSG00000102… NA            
#> 2 ENST00000615611.4 FLT1-206        protein_coding  ENSG00000102… NA            
#> 3 ENST00000617835.4 FLT1-208        protein_coding  ENSG00000102… NA            
#> 4 ENST00000543394.2 FLT1-205        protein_coding  ENSG00000102… NA            
#> 5 ENST00000540678.2 FLT1-203        protein_coding  ENSG00000102… NA            
#> 6 ENST00000541932.5 FLT1-204        protein_coding  ENSG00000102… NA            
#> # ℹ 16 more variables: source_transcript_id <chr>, tags <chr>,
#> #   coding_status <chr>, transcript_support_level <chr>, tie_score <dbl>,
#> #   cds_start <int>, cds_end <int>, cds_length <int>, is_canonical <lgl>,
#> #   haplotype <chr>, seqid <chr>, start_pos <int>, end_pos <int>, strand <chr>,
#> #   n_exons <int>, tx_length <int>
